review.alternative: Stability might emerge entirely from reactive feedback without explicit risk measures.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence that systems without time-consistent risk measures achieve equivalent stability under high uncertainty.

claims.statement: Autonomous safety architectures rely on rigorous, time-consistent risk measures to stabilize decision outcomes in dynamic, unpredictable environments.

support.explanation: The source discusses how risk-sensitive Model Predictive Control provides provably stabilizing behavior across risk preferences.
support.passage: a full range of risk preferences from risk-neutral (i.e., expectation) to worst case. Within this framework, we propose and analyze an online risk-sensitive MPC algorithm that is provably stabilizing.

actions.findings: Autonomous safety architectures rely on rigorous, time-consistent risk measures to stabilize decision outcomes in dynamic, unpredictable environments. [source-a499e83cfad44bf6]
actions.limitations: The current synthesis assumes that risk-sensitivity parameters are static; further research must address how these parameters themselves adapt to long-term experience.
actions.next_questions: How do adaptation rates in risk-sensitive architectures alter long-term preference stability?
actions.reason: Updating notebook findings with verified source evidence on risk-sensitive control frameworks.
actions.summary: Stable preference formation in autonomous agents is structurally supported by time-consistent risk measures, such as risk-sensitive Model Predictive Control (MPC), which provide a deterministic basis for decision-making against environmental unpredictability, contrasting with transient behavioral responses.
actions.title: Architectural Distinctions in Preference Formation

review.alternative: Simple modular systems could achieve equivalent accountability without complex integration.
review.would_change_mind: Demonstration of verifiable accountability frameworks operating in non-integrated systems.
